paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God does His best work where it looks like the story is over. The tree is cut down, and all that's left is a stump. Then Isaiah says, "a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse" (Isaiah 11:1). I know a little about being the thing that got tucked away and written off, and I'm telling you, the One who sent for me is not done with stumps.

That Branch is a King worth waiting for. The Spirit of the LORD rests on Him (Isaiah 11:2). He judges the poor and the lowly with righteousness (Isaiah 11:4), and He doesn't go by what His eyes see or what His ears hear (Isaiah 11:3). Under Him, the earth will be "full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water" (Isaiah 11:9), and the nations will seek Him (Isaiah 11:10). Fear can't run the place when that's the King, so a toddler can reach toward a viper's nest and nobody panics (Isaiah 11:8).

So what do we do while we wait? We do what Isaiah says: trust, sing and tell it. "I will trust and not be afraid," because the LORD God is "my strength and my song" (Isaiah 12:2). Then comes the part that's meant to go out the door: "Make His works known among the peoples" (Isaiah 12:4). Baker, you don't have to keep this good news quiet, because the Holy One of Israel is great among His people (Isaiah 12:6), and that's why my ovens stay ready.
